## 1. Overview & Background
Using devices such as Jawbone Up, Nike FuelBand, and Fitbit, it is now possible to collect a large amount of data about personal activity relatively inexpensively. In this project, our goal is to use data from accelerometers on the belt, forearm, arm, and dumbbell of 6 participants who were asked to perform barbell lifts correctly and incorrectly in 5 different ways (`classe` variable). 

The training data contains 19,622 observations across 160 variables, and the testing data consists of 20 unlabelled test cases.

---

## 2. Data Preprocessing & Cleaning
We load the training and testing datasets and clean them by removing near-zero-variance predictors, identification columns, and summary columns with over 90% missing values (`NA`).

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(caret)
library(randomForest)

# Load data
train_url <- "[https://d396qusza40orc.cloudfront.net/predmachlearn/pml-training.csv](https://d396qusza40orc.cloudfront.net/predmachlearn/pml-training.csv)"
test_url  <- "[https://d396qusza40orc.cloudfront.net/predmachlearn/pml-testing.csv](https://d396qusza40orc.cloudfront.net/predmachlearn/pml-testing.csv)"

train_raw <- read.csv(url(train_url), na.strings=c("NA", "#DIV/0!", ""))
test_raw  <- read.csv(url(test_url), na.strings=c("NA", "#DIV/0!", ""))

# Remove columns with more than 90% missing values
valid_cols <- colMeans(is.na(train_raw)) < 0.90
train_data <- train_raw[, valid_cols]
test_data  <- test_raw[, valid_cols]

# Remove metadata columns (timestamps, user names, index)
exclude_cols <- c("X", "user_name", "raw_timestamp_part_1", "raw_timestamp_part_2", 
                  "cvtd_timestamp", "new_window", "num_window")
train_data <- train_data[, !names(train_data) %in% exclude_cols]
test_data  <- test_data[, !names(test_data) %in% exclude_cols]

# Convert target variable 'classe' to factor
train_data$classe <- as.factor(train_data$classe)
